content.text:
I submitted index 94 (Bi 0.09, Cu 0.52, V 0.39) as the best composition. It gave a photocurrent of 4.2e-7 A. I only had 3 measurements for 275 candidates, so it is the best of those three, not a confirmed library maximum.

| Index | Bi / Cu / V | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.24 / 0.18 / 0.58 | 1.6e-7 |
| **94** | **0.09 / 0.52 / 0.39** | **4.2e-7** |
| 110 | 0.17 / 0.51 / 0.32 | 1.8e-7 |

- **Why I sampled these:** the light is 2.4 eV, right at the edge of what BiVO4 absorbs. Copper vanadates absorb light below 2.4 eV, so I compared a composition close to BiVO4 (index 1) with a copper-rich vanadate (index 94).
- **What I found:** the copper-rich, low-bismuth region gave more than twice the photocurrent.
- **Third measurement:** index 110 has more bismuth and less vanadium than 94, and its photocurrent dropped back to 1.8e-7 A. More bismuth in that region doesn't help.
- **Not explored:** compositions richer in copper than 94 at similarly low bismuth, such as 137 or 197, went unmeasured. One of them might beat 94.
- **XRD:** I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, so the choice has no phase data behind it. XRD could have identified which crystal phases were present before I spent the last photocurrent measurement.
